title: Old Book Smell Is The Book Falling Apart

scenes.narration: That amazing old book smell is literally the smell of the book slowly breaking down.
scenes.note: Bill has his face in a book at frame 0, blissful. The reveal turns the bliss into decay.

scenes.narration: As paper, ink, glue, and bindings age, they release volatile chemicals into the air.
scenes.note: Four materials named, four labelled and aged in turn. Rhythmic — one per keyword.

the page stack labels PAPER and yellows
the ink labels and fades brown
the spine glue labels and cracks
the stitching labels and frays
small molecule marks lift off every labelled part and drift upward

scenes.narration: Different compounds can create grassy, musty, almond-like, and even vanilla-like smells.
scenes.note: Four smells, four icons. Each pops on its own word — this is the densest scene in the episode.

scenes.narration: Scientists and conservators can even study these emissions to learn about the condition of aging paper.
scenes.note: The smell becomes data. Scent curls get captured and turned into a readout.
